query: TC4 (Ti6Al4V) is an unmodified α + β dual-phase alloy whose low hardness and poor friction and wear properties limit its use under extreme-service and high-contact-stress conditions. Formulate one hypothesis for an intervention that could improve its hardness and wear resistance without sacrificing its existing beneficial properties. State the intervention, proposed mechanism, predicted outcome relative to untreated TC4, applicable operating or test boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit result that would falsify the hypothesis.

falsification_experiment.design: Comparative study of TC4 titanium alloy with and without Si-reinforced Ti-based composite coatings
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the hardness and wear resistance of the coated TC4 titanium alloy are not significantly improved compared to the untreated alloy, the hypothesis is falsified.

## Abstract
AbstractThe hardness and wear resistance of the surface of TC4 titanium alloy, which is widely used in aerospace and other fields, need to be improved urgently. Considering the economy, environmental friendliness, and high efficiency, Si-reinforced Ti-based composite coatings were deposited on the TC4 surface by the high-speed wire-powder laser cladding method, which combines the paraxial feeding of TC4 wires with the coaxial feeding of Si powders. The microstructures and wear resistance of the coatings were analyzed using X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Vickers hardness tester, and friction and wear tester. The results indicate that the primary composition of the coating consisted of α-Ti and Ti5Si3. The microstructure of the coating underwent a notable transformation process from dendritic to petal, bar, and block shapes as the powder feeding speed increased. The hardness of the composite coatings increased with the increasing Si powder feeding rate, and the average hardness of the composite coating was 909HV0.2 when the feeding rate reached 13.53 g/min.
